issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court’s appellate jurisdiction under Section 125 of the Electricity Act is limited to cases involving a substantial question of law.

Delays in obtaining required approvals caused by government authorities, where the project developer acted diligently and was not negligent, qualify as a force majeure event under the power purchase agreement.

A project developer entitled to force majeure relief is entitled to an extension of the scheduled commissioning date and is not liable for liquidated damages or a reduced tariff under the power purchase agreement.
A contractual late-payment surcharge may be awarded on the restored tariff difference even if the claim was not specifically pleaded.
